messages:
Aisha: Hi folks—my passport and wallet were pickpocketed in Shinjuku last night. I have a 3-day antibiotic prescription the clinic gave me but the pharmacy says they need 'proof of insurance' or an employer confirmation to dispense. Can People Ops send something ASAP?

People Ops: Sorry that happened, Aisha. Yes we can generate a proof-of-coverage/verification letter for the pharmacy. Quick questions: do you want us to email the pharmacy or provide a printable PDF for you? Also we need the pharmacy name, email, and the clinic invoice if you have it. If you only have a receipt photo that's fine.

Aisha: Pharmacy will only accept email from employer. Name: "Sakuraya Pharmacy" — contact email sakuraya@pharm.jp. I have a photo of the clinic invoice (in Japanese) and the prescription slip. Uploading now.

Claims Team: Checklist for international pharmacy releases — please upload the following to the portal under "Foreign/Travel Claims":

- Clinic invoice or prescription copy (photo ok)
- Proof of payment OR credit card txn screenshot if paid
- Short English translation of key invoice lines (medicine name, quantity, price)
- Passport page photo (ID page) OR government ID if passport stolen
- A brief statement describing the theft (1-2 sentences)

Claims Team: Note — for pharmacies we can either email a verification letter or create a signed PDF you can print. If you need the pharmacy to bill us directly wecan attempt to set up a direct-pay but that requires provider agreement and extra steps.

Aisha: Uploaded clinic_receipt.jpg, rx_photo.jpg, passport_page.jpg, theft_statement.txt. Please email sakuraya@pharm.jp and cc me (aisha@redwood.com).

People Ops: Got the upload. We will email them a verification letter within 6 hours. The letter will confirm active coverage dates and include our benefits team phone number for verification. We redact full policy numbers and include a short claim reference: "Redwood Benefits — Verification 1769004321".

Benefits Bot: Reminder: upload via https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Travel & foreign" for fastest processing. For currency conversions we use the FX rate on the service date from XE.com unless a bank statement shows the exact charge.

Aisha: Thank you — quick Q: will reimbursement be in USD? My clinic charged in JPY and the amount on my card shows JPY -> USD conversion; just want to know expected timeline.

Claims Team: Reimbursements are issued in USD. We calculate the USD using the exchange rate on the date of service (XE.com) unless you provide a bank statement showing the card charge in JPY and the converted USD. Timeline: expect initial claim intake confirmation within 48 hours, full processing in 7-14 business days after we receive all docs. Emergency meds verification emails are prioritized.

Kenji Sato: FYI when I had to do this in Osaka they wanted a pharmacy phone number for verification. If email bounces, call them: +81 3 1234 5678 (Sakuraya main). Also ask the pharmacist for the dispensing stamp photo — that helped.

People Ops: Email to sakuraya@pharm.jp sent and cc'd to you — message ID HR-176900-A. We included coverage dates (redacted policy ID), claim ref 1769004321, and benefits phone +1-555-0199 for verification. Copy of the letter uploaded to your benefits portal folder.

Aisha: Sakuraya replied: they need the pharmacy to see a company contact on phone. They requested a call to verify. People Ops — can someone call +81 3 1234 5678 between 09:00-17:00 JST?

People Ops: We can call. @Claims Team will handle verification call and confirm the pharmacist accepts the emailed letter. Will update here after call.

Claims Team: Called and verified with Sakuraya pharmacist (Ms. Tanaka). She confirmed receipt of email and accepted the letter. Pharmacist requested the dispensing stamp photo once meds are given; we asked them to email a scanned dispensing slip to sakuraya@pharm.jp referencing our claim ref.

Aisha: They just dispensed the meds! Pharmacist sent a scanned dispensing slip to sakuraya@pharm.jp and also offered to invoice Redwood directly if we provide a purchase order — is that something we can do?

Claims Team: We can try to arrange direct invoice payment for in-country pharmacies on a case-by-case basis. It requires a signed provider invoice, W-8/W-9 equivalent or local tax docs, and finance approval. For speed, submit the scanned dispensing slip and clinic invoice; we'll process reimbursement. If you want us to pursue direct payment, mark "Direct Pay Request" in the upload note and we will escalate to finance.

People Ops: Closing loop — we uploaded the verification call notes and the pharmacy's dispensing slip to your portal folder. Claim intake logged as "IN-THE-WORKS" and you should get an intake email shortly. If sakuraya wants a PO for direct billing, please say yes and we'll try to enable it, but expect longer processing.

Aisha: Really appreciate the quick help and the call. Saved me from running around. :pray:

Benefits Bot: Tip: enable international travel cover in the portal settings before trips; you'll get a pre-filled PDF with emergency verification to show at counters.
